newsitem.title: CHILE: Chile shares end lower, power sector wobbly.
newsitem.headline: Chile shares end lower, power sector wobbly.

text.p: Chilean shares closed down in light trade with the market dominated by concerns that electricity sector profits will be hurt by lower prices and a drought in central Chile, said traders.
The market could open firm with prices driven higher by the tight liquidity, they said.
The 40-share IPSA index ended off 0.25 percent at 96.91 points. The general IGPA index moved down 0.5 percent to 5,297.43 points.
Turnover shrank to 7.7 billion pesos from 10.6 billion pesos Thursday.
Traders reported a wave of selling by foreign investors of Chilean-issued American Depositary Receipts, especially of stocks in the power sector.

Power stocks, which account for a 40 percent weighting in the IPSA index, have been hammered over recent weeks by cuts in generating prices and a legal dispute over government plans to slash distribution rates.
But electricity shares are expected to be buoyed next week by news that a group including Chilectra has prequalified in the sale of Brazilian utility Cerj, said dealers.
"It's good news for the electricity firms as it's clear the situation is bad for them here," said one dealer.
Generators have also been hit by a severe drought which has lowered water levels in dams in central Chile.
Chilgener lost 0.44 percent to 2,280 pesos, while Enersis shed 0.42 percent to 239-1/2 pesos.
Winners included winery Concha y Toro, up 2.35 percent at 174 pesos, copper products maker Madeco, up 1.04 percent at 970 pesos, and telecom Telex, which rose 0.84 percent to 1,185 pesos.
